Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 60,00,000/- from the date of accident till its realization for the fatal injury sustained by Mohd. Shakil MACP No. 816/18; FIR No. 399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 Saifi, aged about 27 years in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 22.12.2016 at about 4:00 PM at Dhummanikpur Bypass, PS. Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar, involving Bus bearing registration no. UP15-BT-9141 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 22.12.2016, deceased Md. Sakeel Saifi was going to Dhummanikpur bypass from Kidwai Nagar, Dadri, Gautam Budh Nagar on motorcycle bearing registration no. DL3S-BQ-1864 which was being driven by him at a normal speed and on correct side of the road.

At about 4:00 pm, when he reached at Dhummanikpur Bypass, PS. Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar, offending vehicle i.e., Bus bearing registration no. UP15-BT- 9141 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high, in a rash and negligent manner and in a zigzag manner, came from Sikandrabad side and hit against the motorcycle of deceased with a great force, as a result of which, deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Mohan Swaroop Hospital, in front of Peer ke paas, G.T. Road, Dhoom Dadari, Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar, Delhi, where doctor declared him 'brought dead'.
His postmortem was conducted at District Mortuary, Gautam Budh Nagar vide PMR No. 1313/2016 dated 23.12.2016.
A case U/s 279/304A/427 IPC was registered at PS. Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar vide FIR No. 399/16 with regard to the accident MACP No. 816/18; FIR No. 399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned Sabana And Ors (Lrs Of Mohd. Shakil) vs Sunil Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136247093/

In its written statement, the respondent no. 2/UPSRTC has claimed that on 22.12.2016, alleged offending vehicle Bus No. UP15-BT- 9141 was plying on Kanpur-Delhi route at around 15:30 hrs and when the bus reached Dadri Bypass, a motorcyclist riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and crossing the turn, got hit by one unknown car and motorcyclist lost control and fell down on the road and suffered grievous injuries.

It has claimed that when the driver of alleged offending vehicle saw the incident, applied his mind and took the bus on the side of the road and meanwhile the car driver ran away from the spot and police falsely implicated the bus driver and registered a false and frivolous case against the driver of the bus.
It has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order dated 08.07.2019:-
1) Whether the deceased Mohd. Shakil Saifi died in road traffic accident on 22.12.2016 at about 4:00 PM at Dhummanikpur Bypass, PS. Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Badalpur, due to rash and negligent driving of UP Roadways Bus No. UP15-BT-9141 by its driver namely Sunil Kumar / R-1 which was owned by UP State Road/R- 2?OPP.
2) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP.
3) Relief.

8.
For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW2 Sh. Islamuddin Saifi (alleged eyewitness) is relevant.
He deposed in his evidence that he was the eyewitness in the present case as well as father of deceased Mohd. Shakil Saifi.
He further deposed that on the day of accident, his son was coming from Ghaziabad to give him a mobile phone on Dhummanikpur Bus Stand.
He further deposed that he was waiting for his son, meanwhile the accident had taken place and many people gathered over there.
He further deposed that when he reached at the spot, he saw the person who met with an accident was his son Mohd. Shakil Saifi.
He further deposed that with the help of public persons, he took his son to the hospital where he was declared brought dead.
He further deposed that the accident took place due to negligence on the part of bus driver.

9. During his cross-examination on behalf of driver and owner, he deposed that the bus no.
UP15-BT-9141 hit his son.
He denied the suggestion that he had not seen the accident.
He further deposed that his deceased son was returning from his relative's house at the time of accident.
He denied the MACP No. 816/18; FIR No. 399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 suggestion that the deceased was driving his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.
He further denied the suggestion that the bus driver was not negligent in causing the accident.

10. It is evident from the testimony of PW2 that the insurance company could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Moreover, FIR No. 399/16 is shown to have been registered on the statement of this witness i.e. PW2 Sh. Islamuddin.
The contents of said FIR would show that he had disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident, as deposed by him as PW1 during the course of inquiry.
11. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the criminal case, have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely Sunil Kumar has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s. 279/304A/427 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

12. No doubt, the respondents no. 1 & 2 have examined themselves MACP No. 816/18; FIR No.
399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 as R1W1 and R1W2 during the course of inquiry.

So far as, the testimony of respondent no. 2(R2W1 who is AR of respondent no. 2) is concerned, same is of no relevance for the purpose of this issue as he was undisputedly not present at the time of accident.

On the other hand, R1W1(respondent no. 1 has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. R1W1/A that there was no rash and negligent driving on his part while driving vehicle bearing registration no.
UP15-BT-9141.

He further deposed that when he reached at Dadri Bypass, saw a motorcyclist riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and while crossing the turn, he got hit by one unknown car and lost his control, fell down and sustained injuries.

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderence of probabilities that Smt. Reena Devi had sustained fatal injuries in the road accident which took place on 22.12.2016 at about 4:00 PM at Dhummanikpur Bypass, PS. Badalpur, District Gautam Budh MACP No. 816/18; FIR No.
399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 Nagar, due to rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Thus, this issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
19. The petitioners who are claimants are the widow, three minor children and parents of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

20. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals MACP No. 816/18; FIR No. 399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation &
Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
21. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

During cross-examination of PW1 (mother of deceased) on behalf of driver and owner, she deposed that her permanent residence was of Dadri, UP but at that time they were residing at Bhalswa Dairy in a rented accommodation.
She further deposed that she had not filed any document showing her address of Bhalswa Dairy.
She further deposed that she did not know as to in which company his son was working.
Counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that income of deceased should be considered as Rs. 23,000/- per month.
He further argued that since deceased was not having permanent job and he was aged about 30 years at the time of accident, future prospects @ 40% should also be awarded in favour of the petitioners.

25. In order to prove the employment and income of deceased, petitioners have examined PW3 Sh.
Praveen Kumar Jain from the office of employer of deceased who has produced the salary statement of deceased for the month of November, 2016 and exhibited the same as Ex. PW3/A.

He further deposed that the aforesaid salary slip had been issued by the bank after their request vide Sabana And Ors (Lrs Of Mohd. Shakil) vs Sunil Kumar on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136247093/

He further deposed that the said salary had been duly reflected in the payslip Ex. PW3/A.
He further deposed that the company had issued the salary certificate to the wife of deceased which was already on record Ex. PW1/1.
During his cross-examination on behalf of driver and owner, he deposed that he had not brought any record of the deceased except the aforesaid salary slip.
He admitted that the salary for one month only had been reflected in the payslip Ex. PW3/A.
He deposed that he had not brought the appointment letter of the deceased.
He denied the suggestion that he had filed the false and fabricated documents.
He further deposed that he could not tell as to whether the salary of the deceased employee was being disbursed directly in his bank account.
He further deposed that there was 1200 employees approximately working in the company and the salary of all the employees were disbursed directly in the bank account of the employees.
He deposed that the deceased had joined their company in April, 2015.
He further deposed that after joining his duties, the deceased had stopped to report for duty on regular basis.
He further deposed that the services of the deceased were then regularized from mid June 2015.
He denied the suggestion that the bank statement Ex. PW3/A was false and fabricated document.
He further denied the suggestion that deceased was not working with them at the time of accident.

26. After referring to the testimonies of PW1 & PW3 and the documents filed by the petitioners, Ld.
counsel for petitioners vehemently MACP No. 816/18; FIR No. 399/16 DOD:04.06.2025 argued that last drawn monthly salary of deceased may be taken as Rs. 23,000/- in order to calculate the loss of dependency.
27. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondent no. 2 argued that there is no concrete evidence led by petitioners to establish the monthly income of deceased at the time of accident.
Thus, loss of dependency should be calculated on the basis of notional income as per Minimum Wages Act applicable during the relevant period.
28. As per the the documents produced by PW3, it is apparent that deceased Shakeel Saifi was working with Ashtech Industries Pvt Ltd at the time of accident.
It may be noted here that petitioners have relied upon salary certificate (Ex. PW1/1) of deceased.

As per the document Ex.
PW3/A, an amount of Rs. 23,000/- was deposited in his bank account of deceased by Ashtech on 14.12.2016.

The date of accident in the present case is 22.12.2016 and the salary record (Ex. PW3/A)
produced by PW3 is of the month December, 2016.

In view of the aforesaid and after referring to the testimonies of PW1 & PW3, I deem it fit to accept the monthly salary of deceased as Rs. 23,000/-
per month on average basis.

I am fortified in my view with the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in case titled "Mohammed Siddique & Anr. Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 79 of 2020, decided on 08.01.2020.

sentences.text: But unfortunately the High Court thought that the employer should have produced salary vouchers and other records including income tax returns, to substantiate the nature of the employment and the monthly income.

On the ground that in the absence of other records, the salary certificate and the oral testimony of the employer could not be accepted, the High Court proceeded to take the minimum wages paid for the unskilled workers at the relevant point of time as the benchmark.
17. But we do not think that the approach adopted by the High court could be approved.

To a specific question in crossexamination, calling upon PW2 to produce the salary vouchers, he seems to have replied that his business establishment had been wound up and that the records are not available.
This cannot be a ground for the High Court to hold that the testimony of PW2 is unacceptable.
18. The High Court ought to have appreciated that the Court of first instance was in a better position to appreciate the oral testimony.
So long as the oral testimony of PW2 remained unshaken and hence believed by the Court of first instance, the High Court ought not to have rejected his evidence.
After all, there was no allegation that PW2 was set up for the purposes of this case.
There were also no contradictions in his testimony.

As against the testimony of an employer supported by a certificate issued by him, the High Court ought not to have chosen a theoretical presumption relating to the minimum wages fixed for unskilled employment.
Therefore, the interference made by the High Court with the findings of the Tribunal with regard to the monthly income of the deceased, was uncalled for.
Xxxxx 29.
As per the case of petitioners, deceased Shakeel Saifi was aged about 27 years at the time of accident.
It is pertinent to note that petitioners have filed copy of 10th class marksheet (which is part of Ex. PW1/2) of deceased wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 20.07.1986.
Thus, he was more than 30 years but less than 31 years as on the date of accident(date of accident being 22.12.2016).

Hence, the multiplier of 17 would be applicable in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation", 2009 ACJ 1298 SC which has been reaffirmed by the pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors.", passed in SLP(Civil) No. 25590/14 decided on 31.10.17.

PW1 Smt. Mahamudan has categorically deposed in her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A)
that all the petitioners were dependent upon the deceased at the time of accident.
It is relevant to mention here that said part of her testimony remained unchallanged.

In view of the same, it is held that there were six dependents upon the deceased i.e. widow, three minor children and parents of deceased at the time of accident and there has to be deduction of one fourth as held in the case of Sarla Verma mentioned supra.

Thus, the total loss of dependency would come out to Rs.
49,26,600/- (Rs. 23,000/- X 3/4 X 140/100 X 12 X 17).
Hence, a sum of Rs. 49,26,600/- is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.
20. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
The aforesaid Principle of law has also been reiterated by a landmark judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme court in 2017 (13) SCALE 12 : 2017 XI AD (SC) 113 titled National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.
Accordingly, the quantum of appropriate and adequate compensation to the victim of road accident is to be derived after assessment of various relevant parameters, as per law.
The date of accident in the present case is 22.12.2016 and the salary record (Ex. PW3/A)
produced by PW3 is of the month December, 2016.
In view of the aforesaid and after referring to the testimonies of PW1 & PW3, I deem it fit to accept the monthly salary of deceased as Rs. 23,000/-
per month on average basis.
I am fortified in my view with the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in case titled "Mohammed Siddique & Anr. Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 79 of 2020, decided on 08.01.2020.
On the ground that in the absence of other records, the salary certificate and the oral testimony of the employer could not be accepted, the High Court proceeded to take the minimum wages paid for the unskilled workers at the relevant point of time as the benchmark.
To a specific question in crossexamination, calling upon PW2 to produce the salary vouchers, he seems to have replied that his business establishment had been wound up and that the records are not available.
This cannot be a ground for the High Court to hold that the testimony of PW2 is unacceptable.
18. The High Court ought to have appreciated that the Court of first instance was in a better position to appreciate the oral testimony.
So long as the oral testimony of PW2 remained unshaken and hence believed by the Court of first instance, the High Court ought not to have rejected his evidence.
After all, there was no allegation that PW2 was set up for the purposes of this case.
There were also no contradictions in his testimony.
As against the testimony of an employer supported by a certificate issued by him, the High Court ought not to have chosen a theoretical presumption relating to the minimum wages fixed for unskilled employment.
Therefore, the interference made by the High Court with the findings of the Tribunal with regard to the monthly income of the deceased, was uncalled for.
Hence, the multiplier of 17 would be applicable in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation", 2009 ACJ 1298 SC which has been reaffirmed by the pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors.", passed in SLP(Civil) No. 25590/14 decided on 31.10.17.
